note: SPACE-008 preserve source manifest: M09's plan answers what is under a directory minus what a build regenerates, which is a different question from what may leave the machine. src/selfhost/manifest_policy.zig makes both explicit: required inputs are kept even when the checkout's ignore rules would drop them (generated source a build needs is exactly this case), and prohibited paths are excluded even when present, because presence is not permission. A path that is both required and prohibited is refused rather than resolved - guessing which instruction wins is how secrets travel. A required input missing from the checkout is named rather than producing a silently incomplete snapshot. Prohibition rules are matched against normalized paths, so src/../.env is still prohibited, and containment compares whole components so a sibling beginning with the word 'secrets' is not excluded. The preview carries a reason per entry, so the list is readable before anything is copied. Running it found a real double free: the missing-required-input path hand-freed the partial lists that the errdefers already own; my disguised-path fixture also omitted the manifest's required inputs and was corrected rather than the code. Fault proof: matching no prohibition rule makes the exclusion assertions fail (exit 1; the first fault attempt did not compile, which is a compile error and not a fault, and was retaken); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
